original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: Credit binding for one idle-axis hosted residual: sufficient entry/exit gauges for the hosting move (S' inside the pending set S, no intervening touch of the host between the residual application and the advance, pairwise disjoint hosted blocks, host endpoint prescribed by the advance), stated as sufficient legality hypotheses of the inherited hosting interface rather than a necessary condition for operator equality (cancellation routes such as the consecutive touches T, T^{-1} past a moved factor R = I + E01 remain open), and a per-cut credit allocation for the claimed hosting credit against the history-span endpoint term H_end, audited on the smallest complete instances in the scalar common-frame transport model of PR 1664 (pull/1664) PROOF.md sections 4-5.
scope_change_reason: The drawn persistent-boundary object (consecutive dirty-connector calls) is covered by open concurrent PR https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1739 (1337isnot1337) and the adjacent-call centre-fanout claim posted 2026-10-14T11:11Z in https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1516. This task instead takes the explicit open request https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18916098 (an664) and PR 1664's open next questions 1-2, keeping the card's method-2 shape: a lower bound on the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface (the idle-axis hosting window contract).
bottleneck_link: Hosting credit is the accounting that lets the coverage law count work as eliminated boundary work; without a gauge binding, a claimed hosting credit can exceed what the host's compulsory displacement pays. The receipt pins credit <= H_end for restored hosts and isolates the one endpoint-contract change (absorption) that could credit more, which is the quantity the coverage-law/unpaid-coordinate line changes.
stop_rule: One bounded interface receipt: smallest falsifying instance first, one exhaustive toy family (156 regions), four gauge controls, then stop. No supplier replay, no kappa target.
evidence: python3.12 -B research/dirty-host-gauge-binding-seedea2e/verify.py prints PASS_DIRTY_HOST_GAUGE_BINDING: the double-duty borrow and the absorbed-endpoint-with-separate-target are refuted at cut 1 by exactly one direction (count and span feasibility); full absorption alone passes and is flagged as a contract change; three dropped-gauge counterexamples for the sufficient operator hypotheses (each cannot simply be deleted, none proved necessary) plus the cancellation regression control R = I + E01, T = I + E12, T^{-1} = I - E12, where both touches fail to commute with R yet T^{-1} T R = R T^{-1} T = R and the sufficient-only condition accepts the equality; the PR1664 section 5.2 arithmetic reproduced with an M<=6 mutant refuted; pre-positioned dirt earns no credit; and all 156 enumerated restored-host regions satisfy (C-down) and the exact identity sum_j need_j = q*rank(S) + H_end.
